_doc: Risk classification for the /test --instructions gate.
Categories:
safe              - read-only; no host effect. Default for type=question/query.
mutating          - changes server-side state or agent metadata in the test stack;
safe to run against a UAT stack.
destructive       - modifies host filesystem, registry, services, or runs arbitrary
code. NOT run by default --instructions mode.
network-disrupt   - disconnects host network; only run inside the quarantine
ceremony (PR B).
interactive       - pops UI on the host; opt-in only.
forensic          - the server refuses a broadcast and requires exactly one explicit
in-scope agent_id (dispatch_destructive_gate.hpp); the runner
broadcasts, so these are opt-in only. Source of truth: the Forensics
rows in server/core/src/capability_decls/*.hpp.
server-internal   - catalog-only definitions with no agent plugin (plugin _server,
server, server_internal). The dispatch chokepoint denies them
(reason=unclassified or forbidden), so they cannot pass by dispatch.
The plugin rule classifies them; list an id here only to override it
(for example a destructive server definition).
The runner dispatches broadcasts only (no agent_ids, no scope). A definition on a
Destructive or Forensics capability row, and a server-internal one, therefore cannot
pass when selected with --risks: the server answers HTTP 400 or 503. Those classes are
classification-only until the runner can supply explicit targets.
Default rule (applied if id not listed below):
- plugin _server, server or server_internal -> server-internal
- spec.type=question or spec.type=query -> safe
- spec.type=action                      -> mutating
This file is the AUTHORITY: an explicit override here always wins over the default.
When you add a new InstructionDefinition, classify it here if it is anything
other than 'safe' or 'mutating'. tests/test_instructions_risk_table.py fails the
docs suite when a definition on a Destructive or Forensics row is misclassified.
